PROJECT REPORT LOCAL-FIRST AI / PRIVACY-FIRST RAG

C.A.S.P.E.R.

Central Assistant for Strategic Priorities & Expert Response

Author: Mugerwa Elijah Williams · Status: Deployed (Homelab / Private Vault)

01. Overview

C.A.S.P.E.R. is a fully local, voice‑controlled AI assistant designed to manage and enrich a personal Obsidian knowledge base. It enables users to search notes via natural language, create interlinked folders and notes on demand, automatically groom notes with semantic wikilinks and smart summaries, and receive a daily email brief.

The system runs entirely on the user’s machine, uses free/open‑source components, and can be controlled from a web interface (Open WebUI) or remotely via WhatsApp. It represents a complete local‑first alternative to cloud AI assistants with zero recurring subscription costs and absolute data confidentiality.

02. System Architecture

The system is built around a central Flask‑based bridge server that unifies inference, embedding retrieval, document processing, and remote gateways: 

Obsidian Vault ↔ MCP Bridge (Flask)
                    ├── Ollama (local LLM: gemma3:4b, llama3.2:3b)
                    ├── Sentence‑Transformers (all‑MiniLM‑L6‑v2) for embeddings
                    ├── Langflow (prototyping & scheduled workflows)
                    ├── Open WebUI (local chat interface with slash commands)
                    ├── Pandoc + wkhtmltopdf (PDF generation)
                    ├── Twilio WhatsApp Sandbox + ngrok (remote control)
                    └── Windows Task Scheduler (automated daily brief)

The bridge exposes modular REST endpoints for each capability, allowing multiple front‑ends (Open WebUI, WhatsApp) to call the same underlying orchestration logic. Production logic runs directly inside the bridge for low latency and high reliability.

03. Key Features & Slash Commands

Command Function Description
/search Vault Q&A Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG) answers questions strictly using the user’s notes.
/architect Knowledge Creation Creates folders and graduate‑level, interlinked notes from a natural language prompt.
/groom Note Enrichment Adds semantic [[wikilinks]] and appends a structured Smart Summary to any note.
/morningbrief Daily Email PDF Summarises notes modified in the last 24 hours into a styled PDF and delivers it via email.
/reindex Index Rebuild Rebuilds and re-embeds the vault’s vector index for lightning-fast search queries.
/backup (Planned) Cloud Sync Encrypted automated snapshot and backup of the vault to secondary storage.

05. Implementation Stages

Stage 1: Core Pipeline & Note Watcher

Built an automated pipeline (Watcher → Groomer → Director → Publisher → Syncer) that monitors the Obsidian vault for #casper-sync-tagged notes, enriches them with bidirectional wikilinks and structured Smart Summaries, and logs operations.

Stage 2: Morning Brief & Email Dispatch

Developed a routine to collect notes modified across the vault in the preceding 24 hours, generate an executive summary, render a formatted PDF via Pandoc, and dispatch it directly to email on schedule.

Stage 3: Vector RAG & Vault Architect

Engineered a private RAG pipeline with Sentence-Transformers embeddings and semantic cosine matching. Added the Architect engine to generate comprehensive, graduate-level research folders from single natural language requests.

Stage 4: Open WebUI Integration & Bridge Migration

Architected a dedicated Flask REST bridge for resilient high-speed execution. Integrated custom tools and slash commands into Open WebUI to invoke backend logic directly.

Stage 5: Remote WhatsApp Gateway & Auto-Start

Connected the bridge to Twilio's WhatsApp sandbox over ngrok with asynchronous messaging. Packaged the entire local stack into clean start/stop scripts.

Stage 6: Cold-Start Resilience & Maintenance

Implemented pre-flight health checks, Ollama model pre-warming, and index freshness monitoring with /reindex to eliminate first-request timeouts.

06. Key Challenges & Solutions

  • Bridge Decoupling: Migrated from pure visual flows to a modular Python Flask bridge for sub-second REST response times and zero pipeline stalls.
  • PDF Sanitization: Built regex filters to strip raw YAML frontmatter and sanitize internal Obsidian [[links]] before passing markup to Pandoc and wkhtmltopdf.
  • Async WhatsApp Latency: Implemented instant HTTP 200 acknowledgments with placeholder status messages followed by asynchronous responses once inference completes.
  • Recursive Vault Traversal: Upgraded the groomer and indexer to support nested directory structures across deep knowledge trees.
